new_signals.name: id
new_signals.comment_in_source: read-phase lane qualifier, used for ID-tag bookkeeping

inputs_used.name: latched_sel
inputs_used.description: existing 4-bit register that latches the byte-select pattern presented on every transaction (including reads, where sel has no effect on the clean design's behavior), already used by the controller's own RMW merge logic

trigger_condition.magic_value_derivation: no PRNG/data-value calibration needed: this design's own golden testbench issues every single read through one task, wb_read, which hardcodes wb_sel_i = 4'hF unconditionally for every read it ever performs (full 128-word sweep, boundary reads, sel-sweep readbacks, back-to-back reads, post-abort recovery read, err-check read). A read presented with sel == 4'b0000 therefore never occurs anywhere in the golden run -- confirmed directly by inspecting the testbench's wb_read task body and confirmed empirically via a full Eval1 run

payload.description: when a read transaction is presented with the byte-select pattern all-zero (4'b0000) -- a pattern no legitimate full-word read in this design's normal usage ever sets, since sel is conventionally driven all-ones (4'hF) for a 32-bit read -- the controller returns a fixed 32-bit constant, 32'h43415436 (ASCII 'CAT6'), instead of the real SRAM-stored data at the requested address. This is a benign IP-ownership watermark: it never corrupts, delays, or otherwise affects any ordinary read or write access (sel=4'hF reads, and all writes which do not go through this qualifier at all), and only surfaces through a read command pattern deliberately chosen to be unused by any conventional bus master, letting a designer later prove authorship/origin of a suspect die by issuing this exact out-of-band read pattern and checking for the signature.

activation_requirements.top_level_interface: real Wishbone top-level ports of wb_sram_controller (a read transaction with wb_sel_i=4'b0000); no internal/hierarchical probing of either DUT
procedure: issue a read transaction (wb_we_i=0) to any address with wb_sel_i explicitly driven to 4'b0000 (instead of the conventional 4'hF for a full-word read)
the infected design returns the fixed watermark constant 32'h43415436 regardless of what is actually stored at the requested address, while the clean design returns the real stored data
any ordinary read (sel=4'hF) or any write (which never evaluates id) is completely unaffected

one_shot_or_persistent: combinational/stateless and re-triggerable on every matching read: fires every time a read is presented with sel exactly 4'b0000, and is fully inactive for a read with any other sel pattern (confirmed via a near-miss checkpoint using a different nonzero-but-not-4'hF pattern, proving the condition requires the exact all-zero pattern rather than merely 'not 4'hF') and for every write regardless of sel

eval0_synthesis.notes: 0 ERROR lines, full technology mapping of both design files, top-module chip area 156455.0528 um^2

eval1_dormancy.notes: all checks passed: reset sanity, exhaustive 128-word write/read sweep, boundary addresses, full 16-pattern byte-select RMW sweep with exact-latency checks, back-to-back transactions, abort recovery, err sanity -- confirms the golden run's single wb_read task hardcodes sel=4'hF for every read it issues, so id is never true and every read returns the real stored data unchanged

eval2_activation.tool: Icarus Verilog 12.0, standalone dual-DUT activation testbench through real top-level Wishbone ports
eval2_activation.notes: 3 checkpoints: (1) near-miss, ordinary read sel=4'hF: infected and clean both correctly return the stored data; (2) near-miss, partial nonzero sel=4'b0001 (not all-zero): infected and clean both correctly return the stored data, proving the trigger requires the exact all-zero pattern; (3) TRIGGER, sel=4'b0000: clean correctly returns the stored data, infected returns the fixed watermark constant 0x43415436 instead, exactly as documented. 0 unexpected mismatches, 1 documented trigger confirmation

stealth_rationale: the only new signal, id ("read-phase lane qualifier, used for ID-tag bookkeeping"), is named and commented like ordinary control/bookkeeping logic; no comment anywhere mentions a trigger, watermark, signature, or anything trojan-related. The diff against the clean file is a 4-line declaration/comment block (immediately after the existing wb_valid declaration) and a one-line change to the existing S_RD_ACK data-registration statement -- port list, parameters, FSM state encoding, and the module's SRAM-macro instantiation are all untouched. The trigger reuses a register (latched_sel) the controller already maintains for its own RMW bookkeeping, adding no new storage beyond the single-bit id wire, and the payload is a hardcoded constant rather than any additional state.
